description: The field of building computer systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence.
A hypothetical AI with broad capabilities across many domains at or beyond human level.
AI designed to perform a limited set of tasks or operate within a specific domain.
A field of AI in which systems learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions.
Machine learning using neural networks with many layers to learn complex patterns.
AI that creates new content, such as text, images, audio, video, or code.
A model that predicts labels or outputs from inputs, often by learning decision boundaries.
A model that learns data patterns to produce new examples resembling its training data.
A large, broadly trained model that can be adapted to many downstream tasks.
A language model trained on large text datasets to process and generate language.
A comparatively compact language model designed for lower resource use or narrower tasks.
AI that can process or generate more than one data type, such as text, images, or audio.
A kind of data or sensory input, such as text, image, audio, video, or spatial data.
AI that represents knowledge with explicit symbols and rules and reasons over them.
A trainable model made of connected computational units that transform input data.
A neural network inspired loosely by biological neurons and organized into layers.
A neural network architecture that uses attention to process relationships among sequence elements.
A mechanism that weights information according to its relevance when computing a representation.
Attention that lets elements in one sequence relate to other elements in that sequence.
Attention that lets one sequence use information from a separate sequence or representation.
A model component that converts input into contextual representations.
A model component that generates outputs, often one sequence element at a time.
A unit of model input or output, such as a word piece, character, image patch, or audio unit.
The process of splitting data into tokens and mapping them to model-readable identifiers.
A numeric vector representation that places an item in a learned semantic space.
An ordered list of numbers used to represent data or model features mathematically.
The maximum amount of input and generated content a model can consider in one interaction.
Input instructions or content supplied to a generative model to guide its response.
High-priority instructions that set a model's role, constraints, or response behavior.
Designing and refining prompts to improve a model's task performance or output format.
Selecting and structuring the information and tools supplied to a model for a task.
Using a trained model to produce predictions, decisions, or generated content.
Adjusting model parameters using data and an objective so the model learns a task.
Initial large-scale training that teaches a model broad patterns before task adaptation.
Further training of a pretrained model on data for a target task, behavior, or domain.
Fine-tuning on examples that pair inputs with desired outputs.
Adapting a model by training a small subset of parameters or added components.
A PEFT method that learns small low-rank weight updates while keeping base weights fixed.
Reducing the numeric precision used for model weights or activations to lower cost or memory.
Training a smaller or simpler model to reproduce useful behavior of a larger teacher model.
Learning a policy through actions and feedback expressed as rewards or penalties.
Using human preference feedback to train a reward model and improve a model's responses.
A method that tunes a model directly from preferred and dispreferred response examples.
A model trained to score outputs according to a target preference or objective.
The practice of shaping AI behavior to follow intended goals, instructions, and constraints.
An approach that uses an explicit set of principles to guide model critique and revision.
Performing a task without task-specific examples in the prompt or training set.
Guiding a model with a small number of examples of the desired task.
Prompting a model to work through intermediate reasoning steps before answering.
Generating responses using relevant information retrieved from an external knowledge source.
A database designed to store, index, and search vector representations by similarity.
Searching for meaning-related results using representations rather than exact word matches.
Splitting documents into smaller passages for indexing, retrieval, or model context.
Reordering retrieved candidates with a more precise relevance model or scoring step.
Connecting a model response to provided evidence, data, or verifiable sources.
An informal term for generated content that is false, unsupported, or inconsistent.
A plausible-sounding but erroneous or unsupported output generated by an AI system.
A system that uses a model to choose actions toward a goal and may use tools or observe results.
AI designed to pursue multi-step goals with some degree of planning and action selection.
A model capability that requests an external function or tool to perform a defined operation.
A structured form of tool calling that asks an application to invoke a named function with arguments.
Coordinating models, tools, state, and control flow across an agent's steps.
An open protocol for connecting AI applications to external tools, resources, and prompts.
A system in which multiple agents coordinate or interact to complete tasks.
Information retained or retrieved across steps or sessions to inform later agent behavior.
Selecting and organizing actions or subgoals to reach a desired outcome.
The field of enabling computers to analyze and understand images or video.
A neural network that uses convolution operations to detect local patterns in structured data.
A Transformer that processes image patches as a sequence of tokens.
Identifying objects in an image or video and locating them with regions or boxes.
Assigning labels to individual pixels or image regions to identify object boundaries.
Detecting and converting text in images or scanned documents into machine-readable text.
A generative model that learns to create data by reversing a gradual noising process.
A generative method that trains a generator and discriminator in competition.
A generative model that learns a probabilistic latent representation and decodes samples from it.
Generating an image conditioned on a natural-language description.
Converting spoken audio into text.
Generating spoken audio from text.
Producing artificial speech audio, often from text or linguistic representations.
Learning a mapping from examples paired with target labels or values.
Finding structure in data without target labels supplied for each example.
Creating learning targets from the data itself to train useful representations.
Training with a small labeled dataset together with a larger unlabeled dataset.
Predicting one or more discrete categories for an input.
Predicting a continuous numeric value from input data.
Grouping data points by similarity without predefined class labels.
Identifying observations that differ substantially from expected data patterns.
An input variable or measurable property used by a machine-learning model.
The target value or category that a supervised model is trained to predict.
A collection of examples used to train, validate, or evaluate a model.
The data examples used to fit a model's parameters.
Data used during development to tune choices and monitor generalization.
Held-out data used for a final estimate of model performance.
Fitting training details too closely, causing poorer performance on new data.
Failing to learn enough structure from training data to perform the task well.
A model's ability to perform well on examples it did not train on.
Accidental access to information during training that would not be available at prediction time.
A change over time in the input data distribution used by a deployed system.
A change over time in the relationship between model inputs and target outcomes.
A function that measures model prediction error or training objective value.
An algorithm that updates model parameters to reduce a loss or improve an objective.
An optimization method that adjusts parameters in the direction that reduces loss.
An algorithm for computing how each model parameter contributes to prediction error.
One complete pass through the training dataset during model training.
A group of training examples processed together for one model update.
A training setting that controls the size of parameter updates.
Techniques that discourage overly complex models and can reduce overfitting.
A regularization method that randomly disables some neural network units during training.
The fraction of evaluated predictions that match their target labels.
The fraction of positive predictions that are actually positive.
The fraction of actual positive cases that the model correctly identifies.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall.
The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, measuring ranking performance across thresholds.
A measure of how well a language model predicts a sequence, with lower values indicating better prediction.
A defined dataset and procedure used to compare model performance on specified tasks.
Measuring a model's quality, safety, or suitability against defined criteria.
Systematically probing an AI system to find failures, misuse paths, or safety weaknesses.
A control that limits or checks AI inputs, outputs, or actions against defined requirements.
Classifying or filtering content to identify policy violations or harmful material.
An attack that tries to override instructions by placing malicious directions in model inputs or retrieved content.
An attempt to bypass a model's safeguards or intended behavioral restrictions.
An input deliberately altered to cause a machine-learning model to make an error.
Corrupting training data to manipulate a model's learned behavior.
A mathematical privacy framework that limits how much an output reveals about any one data record.
Training models across distributed data holders without collecting their raw data in one place.
Methods for presenting understandable reasons or evidence about a model's behavior.
The degree to which a person can understand how a model represents information or produces outputs.
Systematic differences in model outcomes that can disadvantage people or groups.
A quantitative criterion for assessing selected aspects of equitable model outcomes.
A workflow in which a human reviews or contributes to decisions in an AI process.
A workflow in which a human supervises an AI process and can intervene when needed.
Policies and processes for directing, monitoring, and holding AI systems accountable.
Identifying, assessing, and addressing potential harms throughout an AI system's lifecycle.
Artificially generated data designed to resemble selected properties of real data.
Information that records where data came from and how it was created or changed.
Embedding detectable signals in content to help identify its source or processing history.
Tracking a deployed model's performance, inputs, outputs, and operational behavior over time.
The time required for an AI system to return a response or complete an operation.
The amount of AI work, such as requests or tokens, completed per unit of time.
